verdict.tagline: Brutal cooperative melee action marred by severe initial technical hurdles.
for_you_if: you thrive in cooperative melee combat against hordes
you enjoy mastering deep class progression systems
not_for_you_if: you need a reliable offline single-player mode
you require stable connection servers without disconnects
you are sensitive to motion sickness while playing
you object to strict kernel-level anti-cheat software

distortion_flags.sentence: Positive sentiment increases significantly after the initial window as players move past early technical barriers.

 I don't recommend the game on pc, if you're going to pick it up, I'd say grab them console.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe experiencing motion sickness or dizziness while playing.

citations.review_text: This game was fun and visually interesting but it gave me motion sickness, will not be playing anymore.

Short form: Random FPS instability for no reason, motion sickness / sensory overload.

Long form:

After just playing the tutorial, I noticed that the game was way too loud.
Threw me into the game as well without letting me adjust said setting beforehand.

Also, just by playing the Tutorial, I got insanely motion sick, got dizzy, and had a slight headache.
Most possibly because for some reason, camera bobble for weapon hitting and similar was set to high by default...

I also noticed that my FPS sometimes drops from ~130 FPS down to ~20 FPS for absolutely no reason. While this drop was relatively short, it is enough to infuriate one.

claims.claim: Navigation through levels can feel confusing due to the absence of a minimap or quest markers.

citations.review_text:
This game is literally Left4dead2 but fantasy setting. Even some animations of enemies in this game are so reminiscent of those of special zombies.
Smoker = packmaster
Boomer = lifeleech
Charger = Bestigor
The general gameplay too. You select a chapter , traverse through map by following the enemies hordes (no minimap, no arrow telling you where to go) 

You have 5 chars, but like 20 classes all together (5 are behind dlc)

Was shocked to see in-game microtransaction store, but seems comestic only.

There are daily, weekly quests and events.

Overall this game can be grindy and long if you wish, or a short experience if you only focus on the story.
Every char has a talent tree , to unlock the entire tree you need lvl 30. There are different difficulty options too.

I'm just gonna beat the campaign and call it a day (already halfway through act3 and there are 4) For a game that I got for free years ago from steam not the worst experience. 

Reccomended if you wanna kill some time in co-op.

Able to run it in lowest graphic settings, thank you 
For first timer it's confusing like exploring dark maze without light but thanks to the bots, they're very helpful.
Did countable fingers random multiplayer, and it's very fun aside your level is very low (ie. like you're still level 1, with this character and meet random people with higher level than you, it's still fun and they'll carry you).

Need map for showing the way and quest marker i guess.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players enjoy deep combat despite server instability, technical crashes, and dead alternate modes.

claims.claim: Reviewers report unstable servers, host migration issues, and long connection times.

citations.review_text: weak connection, long connection time, wield host bug, stopped maintenance

I've played a lot of horde shooters/slashers, and nothing has the perfect balance of a "dance" like vermintide 2 does. Fundamentals are strong and they never let you down, dodging, blocking/parrying well goes a long way, weapons are fun to use, careers (classes) are actually distinct from each other and have unique, interesting mechanics.

Team work can make the dream work, there are lots of cool synergetic team setups to try out, and whilst the bots aren't gods at the game, they are also worth a mention. Even if you are a solo player, it is possible to comfortably go through all difficulties present, as the bots are fully customizable and can be made into a team that is quite supportive and tanky. Game is quite well optimized graphically, i run it 60FPS at 2K, no frame gen (can do more but i choose to stay at 60), whilst maxing out everything possible, and it barely takes 50% GPU load.

Outside of gameplay, characters have great depth to them, you will hear dialogue very often, and the banter is actually interesting, subtly (or loudly) revealing backstories on them. It's warhammer fantasy so there's that too, everything is a vibrant, yet dark medieval fantasy. Designs are top notch, if you're a fan of that era's weaponry, armour and fantasy stereotypes you will love this (knights, wizards, battle priests, you get the idea).
Of course, it has its flaws too such as rather unstable servers on quickplay, with some host migration issues (depends on the host themselves too as the game is P2P), also, small things that have not been patched out over the years, such as niche spots on maps where you can get stuck and the like (you are highly unlikely to get into these spots by accident, never happened to me yet).

Overall though, vermintide 2 has managed to become one of my most memorable games, it is especially fun with friends, but it completely supports anyone without too, and you can get lost in the combat loop for hours.

claims.claim: Solo play relies on customizable AI bots, though reviewers describe them as occasionally annoying or needing tweaks.

citations.review_text:
After 666 hours as a relatively new player, I can honestly say that this game is neat.

Feels kind of like a cross between Left 4 Dead and The Lord of the Rings.
Has over 20 campaign missions as well as another half dozen or so in the rogue-lite mode "the chaos wastes".
5 characters with 3 unique careers each (not counting the dlc careers).
A versus mode (which I haven't played).
All included in the base game.

As a solo player without any friends to play with, the deciding factor between this and Darktide was that Vermintide lets you play solo with bots, whom you can customize the careers, talents and loadouts for. 
The bots aren't great, but they're not the worst either and would be fine with a few tweaks (or if Fat Shark would ever re-sanction the bot improvement workshop mod)

Overall my new favorite game and I would recommend to anyone who likes Left 4 Dead and more in depth first person melee combat.

800+ hours later and I still love this game, but it has its flaws. It’s a blast with friends, but the "meta" can be exhausting because there are only so many ways to play effectively. Solo play is rough (bots are annoying) and randoms are hit-or-miss.

Also, for my Linux friends: it runs well, but watch out for keyboard bindings resetting and occasional crashes. It needs more content/new weapons to fight the burnout!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the Versus and Weaves modes are either unpopulated or inactive.

citations.review_text:
It's a fun, replayable game with a high skill ceiling. If you like constantly refining your gameplay in a game where a 2,000 hour player is immediately distinct from a 200 hour player, this game is for you.

The melee combat feels amazing; it looks and sounds great, and your weapons have a great sense of impact behind them.

The playerbase is mainly concentrated on two modes. The first is Adventure, which involves playing from one of 26 (32 with all paid DLC) missions that are 20-40 minutes each. Adventure maps are well-polished; map-specific softlocks and run-ending bugs are rather rare, and the maps themselves are visually stunning. 

The second populated mode is Chaos Wastes, a rogue-like mode where you play through a set of ~8 smaller levels followed by a final arena battle. Each level grants an opportunity to improve your character's weapons and obtain special modifiers to help overcome the final arena.

The other two modes are either unpopulated (Versus PvP) or are unpopulated and DLC-locked (the Weave Expeditions of the Winds of Magic DLC).

To compare this game with Darktide:
- There is a greater focus on melee combat; most of the game's ranged weapons cannot be used to fight hordes, and enemy melee attacks are 'stickier'; back dodges are less effective, which makes it much harder to kite enemies with your ranged weapon out. Engaging in melee combat also gives temporary HP, which is essential for topping off your health.

- Individual enemies (horde enemies and elites) are more threatening. They hit harder and generally take longer to die than their counterparts in Darktide. You will still get large hordes, but unscripted swarms of elites aren't present (A concrete example for Darktide players: this game's equivalent of a Crusher takes longer to die in straight melee combat, and the game will not send large packs of them after you outside of scripted sequences).

- The AI director can let up if the situation demands it; clutching a game as the last man stand…

Probably the closest spritual successor to Left 4 Dead, just in Melee form.

VS Mode is unplayable/unplayed though. PvE is great. Weaves mode is awful/not played. Chaos Wastes mode is fun roguelike-esque.

It's funny how Vermintide 2 manages to be better at everything compared to darktide. Maybe the graphics aren't as pretty... But bots are less braindead, players are less braindead, classes have substantial gameplay variety that work on higher difficulties... Yes... the highest difficulty is behind a paywall, yes the game has 84 DLCS each for just 2 new maps or horned enemies, yes the versus is dead. BUT the dwarf walks funny and has a minigun (if you pay for it).
